shots.details: Wide exterior. Quiet neighborhood/park edge. Bush sits ordinary in foreground. Distant lights and insects establish the world.
Three teenagers rush into frame, duck behind/near the bush, look back toward approaching trouble, then realize they are still holding the six-pack.

shots.dialogue: We gotta get rid of these.
shots.details: One teen checks the cans. Another tries to quiet a rattling can. They whisper, argue for a beat, and glance toward the bush.
The line is shouted with sudden confidence. Brief reaction from the others before the throw.
Six-pack and loose cans arc toward the bush. One can clips a branch, another lands short, then an open can spills directly onto the foliage.
The bush is initially still. Liquid drips through leaves. A tiny twitch. Another twitch. Then the foliage begins moving in a way that is clearly not wind.
Eyes appear/read through the foliage. Busch rises just enough to establish a face and body language. The transformation is strange but restrained.
Busch looks left, right, then down at the spilled cans. He seems confused about being alive before noticing the teenagers fleeing.
Busch deliberately looks away from the chaos with an awkward, almost embarrassed reaction. This is a standalone comedy beat.
Near-still hold. Tiny sway/blink. Night ambience returns to the foreground.
Hard cut to title. Busch remains subtly present behind/around the lettering.

productionRule: The expanded version adds story and movement before the established title beat while preserving the exact spoken phrase -> throw -> transformation -> look-away -> hold -> title structure.
